messages:
sophie: @channel FYI acme-prod is seeing 502/503 on the hosted API /v1/generate since ~2026-03-15T06:12Z. Customers reporting intermittent 5xx and high tail latency. Request IDs: acme-4a9f2b, acme-4a9f3c, acme-4a9f9d. Can someone triage? :eyes:

alex: I'm on it. Can you paste one full request id and the curl you used? Also did we have any deploys to routing/auth/configdb in the last 30m?

sophie: Example request + response attached below. No deploys on customer side; they say it began suddenly.
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-...\" \
  -H \"X-Request-ID: acme-4a9f2b\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"hello"}'
```
Response captured: 
```json
{"error":{"code":503,"message":"control-plane: auth service returned 502"}}
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot report: routing-policy-service v2.3.1 promoted 2026-03-15T06:05Z by ben. No immediate deploy alerts recorded.

alex: I pulled control-plane ingress and routing logs for `acme-4a9f2b`. Seeing auth session lookup timeout followed by config DB query timeouts. Relevant snippets: 
```
[06:12:18Z] ingress: req=acme-4a9f2b -> forward to auth (10.2.1.5)
[06:12:18Z] auth: ERROR session_lookup failed: timeout (sql: read tcp 10.2.2.7:5432: i/o timeout)
[06:12:18Z] routing: ERROR policy eval failed: configdb query timeout (ctx=acme-4a9f2b)
[06:12:18Z] ingress: returning 502 to client (control-plane dependency 5xx)
```

marc: Noted. ConfigDB connection pool usage has been trending up over the last 48h. v2.3.1 included a change that increases parallel policy evaluations per request; could surface as higher DB concurrency. I'll check DB metrics and pool exhaustion now.

priya: I'm seeing repeated `backend/sql: timeout waiting for connection` in routing-policy logs across multiple instances. Sample stack: 
```
err=sql: connection timeout
at github.com/redwood/routing/policy.(*Store).Get
at github.com/redwood/controlplane/handler.EvaluatePolicy
```
I'll capture pprof and heap if needed.

kevin-oncall: For an immediate mitigation, can we enable a tenant-level static fallback route for acme-prod for 15m and bump the auth session cache TTL to reduce DB hits? Who can approve the temporary policy change? :thinking_face:

ben: I approve the static fallback for acme-prod. If metrics don't improve in 10m, I'll roll back routing-policy-service v2.3.1 to v2.2.8. :shipit:

sophie: Sent customer update: "We're investigating intermittent 5xxs; we've identified elevated config DB load in our routing stack and are applying mitigations (temporary fallback + auth cache). We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." (customer notified)

alex: Added repro steps to our private gist. Logging request ids for failed attempts: acme-4a9f2b, acme-4a9f3c, acme-4a9f9d. Repro curl is the same as above. Next steps: marc to check DB pool and slow queries, priya to gather pprof/heap, kevin to apply TTL/cache tweak, ben to prepare rollback. I'll coordinate and update here. :+1:

priya: Paging DB oncall: @dana-db can you look at connection spikes and pg logs? We're seeing `FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved` in PG around 06:11-06:15Z.

dana-db: Looking now. Initial quick check: two routing-policy pods opened a burst of short-lived connections at 06:10-06:13Z and triggered connection slot exhaustion on the reader pool. Capturing session list and slow queries, will post findings in 5m.

sophie: Update: rollback of routing-policy-service started at 06:22Z. Customer reports error rate dropping. Monitoring for 20m before confirming resolution. Thanks all.

kevin-oncall: Monitoring shows 5xxs for acme-prod dropped from ~7.8% -> 0.6% after rollback and TTL tweak. Keeping the TTL change until we fix root cause. Opening a postmortem and will link config/PRs.

alex: Follow-up action items (owners):
- PR: routing-policy DB client -> use prepared statements + adjust pool config to reduce max-conns (owner: marc)
- Add circuit-breaker around configdb queries and fail-fast for overloaded tenants (owner: priya)
- Enforce hard per-tenant DB connection limit at proxy level (owner: dana-db)
- Customer comms draft and postmortem (owner: sophie)

sophie: Closing thread for now; will reopen if errors reappear. :white_check_mark:
